description: Real-world spreadsheet corpora used to measure the auditor's precision (how often a finding is right) and, where ground truth exists, recall. Workbooks are never committed; only sampled finding cards, labels, and the rendered report are.

spreadsheetbench.name: SpreadsheetBench v0.1 (912 instances)
spreadsheetbench.notes: Workbooks attached to real Excel-forum questions (Ma et al., NeurIPS 2024). Each instance ships an _input workbook and a near-duplicate _answer workbook; the default run uses the 2,732 inputs. Modern, formula-heavy, small files (median 10 KB). Saved by Excel, so cached values are present and value-dependent checks run without LibreOffice.

euses-modified.name: Modified EUSES corpus (Graz University of Technology)
euses-modified.license: Academic use; cite the corpus paper (see homepage)
euses-modified.notes: Real EUSES spreadsheets with one injected formula fault per version. Each .properties file names the faulty cell (FAULTY_CELLS_1=sheet!col!row) and the fault type, so it measures whether the auditor points at a known-bad cell. Files are .xls; convert with LibreOffice before auditing. Not run by default.

fuse.name: FUSE (Common Crawl spreadsheets, xlsx subset)
fuse.notes: 9.4 GB single download with no per-file access; web-sourced diversity from a 2013 crawl. Not fetched by default; intended for a CI or one-off run.
